description: Renovate and Dependabot both run here and must not overlap: two
bots proposing the same bump means two PRs, two CI runs and a
guaranteed conflict on the second merge. The split follows
AGENTS.md -- Renovate owns container image tags and the pinned
tool versions that live in workflow env blocks; Dependabot owns Go
modules, GitHub Actions and the docs pip requirements. The
ignorePaths and the disabled managers below are what enforce it.
Removing either means duplicate PRs, not more coverage.
Note what is NOT in ignorePaths: .github/workflows/. It was, on
the first draft, and it silently disabled both customManagers
below -- they match files in exactly that directory. There is no
overlap to guard against there anyway: Dependabot's
github-actions ecosystem bumps `uses:` references, and Renovate's
github-actions manager is not in enabledManagers, so the only
thing Renovate touches in a workflow is the two pinned tool
versions the custom managers name explicitly.
The three images this repository publishes are built by our own
CI from the commit being released; a bot proposing a bump for
them would be proposing that we deploy a version of ourselves,
which release.yml already handles.
Digest pinning for production-track images (AGENTS.md). A tag
is mutable; a digest is the only thing that makes 'we deployed
v1.2.3' reproducible a year later.
Zensical is alpha and ships several releases per week. Its bump
PRs are the scheduled checkpoint for the i18n and blog
workarounds in issue #13, so they are deliberately NOT grouped
with anything else -- each one gets read on its own. Handled by
Dependabot's pip entry; listed here so a future reader does not
add a second manager for it.
golangci-lint is coupled to the Go version: it parses source
with the go/types of the release it was built with, so a
lagging binary panics rather than missing checks. Its bump has
to be read together with whatever Go version is current, never
merged unseen.
One manager per tool, because depNameTemplate and
datasourceTemplate are per-manager: an earlier draft matched all
three version variables in one entry and labelled every hit
golangci/golangci-lint on github-releases, so a yamllint or
hadolint bump would have been proposed against the wrong project.
HADOLINT_SHA256 sits next to HADOLINT_VERSION and is deliberately
NOT updated -- a bot that bumps a version but not its checksum
produces a PR that fails the sha256sum check, which fails in the
safe direction but still needs a human to finish.
yamllint comes from PyPI, not from a GitHub release.
hadolint. HADOLINT_SHA256 beside it stays manual -- see above.
ESPHome is pinned exactly in the firmware workflow. A minor
bump routinely changes generated C++ and has broken this
firmware's build before, so it is never automerged.
Security fixes do not wait for Monday. This is the one thing
allowed to open a PR off-schedule.
